I wrote a long-form post on Transcending Regret, Problems, and Mistakes, exploring this ~koan:

> "If you had a chance for a do-over, would you choose for everything to go exactly the same?
> If not, you have not yet surrendered."

https://t.co/mY8DDRb1mJ
↓
936386902084784128 [2017-12-01] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 6
Shoutout to @Meaningness, whose writing on the fluid mode was part of what helped me figure some of this stuff out. I think that my post itself is also a contribution to the ongoing quest to articulate meta-systematicity.

===

1119241786612944896 [2019-04-19] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 9
👆
I found this exchange delightful because the suggestion that the universe is stuck to you is simultaneously helpful+true, and clearly absurdly false. It's a cariacature of a dualistic perspective trying to understand non-dualism.

1229946492594642945 [2020-02-19] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 1
Also, caveat: words mean different things contextually. This is just my definition. Well, technically, it's the shared definition we use in the framework for our Goal-Crafting Intensive workshops 👇 but anyway.

https://t.co/8Ghoz8goUL
↓
1229946493676724224 [2020-02-19] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 4
1🛣️ no recognizable state = "trajectory"

This one is kind of odd to start with, because moreso than the others, it doesn't necessarily lead to wasted effort. In fact, if you want to explore, whether a new city or a new industry, simply following your appetite can be lovely!
↓
1229946494666579970 [2020-02-19] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 2
2🛣️ no recognizable state = "trajectory"

However, consider a vague state like "successful business". If you haven't clarified whether that's measured in $, impact, or personal autonomy, it'll be hard to recognize if you're going off-track from what you really care about.
↓
1229946495660691458 [2020-02-19] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 3
3🛣️ no recognizable state = "trajectory"

Robert Fritz's creative tension model & the perceptual control model of the brain both require a comparison between "what is so" & "what is wanted"

Want can be implicit, but works better when explicit! (as long as you don't get fixated)
↓
1229946496684109827 [2020-02-19] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 6 🔁 1
1😣 not desired = "should"

This is classic. A lot of the stuff most people have on their to-do lists is not something they feel any sense of motivation towards. It's more like "I don't want to NOT have done this" (which would mean failing my classes, being fired, paying fees)
↓
1229946497686474753 [2020-02-19] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 4
2😣 not desired = "should"

Even with something like "doing my taxes" though, it's possible to have an orientation that's like "well, given that I will eventually do my taxes, how can I orient towards wanting the spaciousness I know I'll feel when they're done?"
↓
1229946498747654145 [2020-02-19] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 2
3😣 not desired = "should"

Sometimes though, if you reflect on it, you might conclude: this isn't what *I* want, it's what my parents wanted for me. I don't have to do this, and *I'm not gonna.* This could be as small as sending an email or as large as a career change.
↓
1229946499766915074 [2020-02-19] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 2
1👀 not future = "regret"

On one level, obviously "the future" is the only time you can achieve a goal, but peoples' thinking often involves a lot of stressing about the present already being the way that it is, rather than accepting the present and saying "where to from here?"
↓
1229946500752510977 [2020-02-19] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 4
2👀 not future = "regret"

Common example: fitness goals.
Setting a weight goal causes someone to pay more attention to their body, which activates shame and a feeling of "I should already be thinner/stronger!" Hard to stay in touch with the future & the learning process.
↓
1229946501729857541 [2020-02-19] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 2 [(SEED) type=quote_of_root]
3👀 not future = "regret"

What I've said about regret in this thread has mostly been at a very high-level; there's also a mindset-shift available here that is a worthwhile deep-dive as well:

https://t.co/3Pzq3t9oHW
  [Quoting @Malcolm_Ocean: I wrote a long-form post on Transcending Regret, Problems, and Mistakes, exploring this ~koan:  > "If you had a chance for a do-over, would you choose for everything to go exactly the same? > If not, you have not yet surrendered."  https://t.co/mY8DDRb1mJ]
↓
1229946502853865475 [2020-02-19] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 3
1☁️ no action = "dream"

We defined a goal as something that causes you to take action. This is a way to highlight that a lot of people have "goals" that are sort of floating around not actually motivating them to do anything.

"Feeling bad about not doing it" doesn't count 😉
↓
1229946503873138689 [2020-02-19] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 2
2☁️ no action = "dream"

Classic examples are "learn a language or musical instrument" or "

Often dreams are bottlenecked on a decision:
- *which* language or instrument?
- how to get started?
- when to practice?
↓
1229946504808402944 [2020-02-19] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 1
3☁️ no action = "dream"

You might be conflicted or have fears about your goals, in a way that makes it hard to act on them directly. However, they're still goals (not dreams) if you're taking the best action available towards resolving that internal conflict!
↓
1229946505789870080 [2020-02-19] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 3
1🤠 actions just for show = "signalling"

However, sometimes you might be taking actions, but any reasonable assessment shows that those actions aren't ever going to really move the needle on the goal.

Maybe poor strategy, but if you *know* useful actions but don't do them...
↓
1229946506813280257 [2020-02-19] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 3
2🤠 actions just for show = "signalling"

Signalling occurs when someone wants to "be an author" more than they want to actually write, publish, etc. They buy notebooks, spend time in cafés with a blank page open, & talk a lot about writing—all of which are actions, but... 🤨
↓
1229946507799007232 [2020-02-19] @Malcolm_Ocean 💜 3
3🤠 actions just for show = "signalling"

Signalling usually is related to the other failure modes above:
- trajectory: actions aren't going anywhere because no "where" to go
- should: "if I stop trying, people will judge"
- regret: trying to show you care about past mistake
↓

"God will never give you more than you can handle" (as a negative example)

rating.reasoning_summary: This strand traces a multi-year philosophical inquiry into transcending regret through acceptance and 'post-mistake' consciousness. Anchored by Malcolm Ocean's 2017 essay and koan ('If you had a chance for a do-over, would you choose for everything to go exactly the same?'), it evolves from abstract spiritual teaching into lived practice. The discourse is highly dialectical—participants test the concept against real emotional pain (Yatharth's fear of imperfection, Visa's childhood anger), refine the vocabulary ('post-mistake,' 'surrendering to the universe'), and ultimately arrive at practical frameworks distinguishing productive learning from rumination. The strand shows genuine knowledge production: moving from 'regret is spiritually confused' to 'regret can be useful if it teaches new lessons vs repeating old ones.' High cohesion among core participants (Malcolm, Yatharth, CountJ0ecool) across 8 years, with later nodes validating the framework's durability.

essential_tweets.annotation: The Origin: Malcolm's 2017 essay introducing the central koan about do-overs and surrender.
The Sticky Phrase: 'Throw out the whole universe and get a new one'—becomes the meme-anchor for the concept.
Integration: Malcolm weaving regret-transcendence into his Goal-Crafting framework, showing practical application.
CountJ0ecool's Deep Dive: Extended riff on 'fucking around' and surrender, demonstrating how the idea propagates.
The Reincarnation Test: CountJ0ecool's thought experiment pushing the koan to its emotional limit.
Yatharth's Synthesis: 'Living in the universe where you made the mistake' becomes the new vocabulary.
Post-Mistake Framework: Yatharth articulating the shift from 'trying to undo' to 'living with' as the core insight.
The Dialectic Turn: Malcolm introducing nuance—spiritual acceptance vs practical learning from avoidable mistakes.
Emotional Validation: Yatharth applying the framework to fear of judgment, showing therapeutic utility.
Viral Restatement: Lichthauch's 2025 tweet (4.8k likes) showing the idea's penetration into broader discourse.

title: Regret Is Wanting a New Universe (Too Bad It’s Stuck)
summary: The most quotable bit is Malcolm Ocean’s dunk on regret: if you’re regretting, you’re basically saying “we need to throw out the whole universe and get a new one”… and the punchline is “yeah—it’s stuck to you!” He frames it as a non-dual “surrender” koan: if you got a do-over, would you choose for everything to go *exactly the same*? If not, “you have not yet surrendered.” That line becomes the thread’s recurring spell—half spiritual teaching, half meme—especially once Yatharth riffs that any future you want has *this moment* in its past, so wishing otherwise is literally wishing for a different cosmos (Malcolm later adds: replacement is expensive, warranty expired, receipt lost).
